short: HMM phone recognizer (M06) standard and below the group's concurrent decoder; recognition-then-unit-selection output (M08) departs from direct mapping but is tested only on oracle phones.
position: The paper [@hueber2010development] changes two components. Its visual phone recognizer (M06) is standard, a context-independent HMM-GMM like 10 of the 11 prior articulatory-signal recognizers (Appendix), and weaker than the authors' own [concurrent] context-dependent multi-stream decoder [@hueber2009visuo]. Its output route (M08), phone recognition then diphone unit selection, departs from the direct mapping of both prior speech-output studies [@kaburagi1998determination; @engwall2005articulatory], but is standard by rule: no direct-mapping baseline is run and synthesis is tested only on oracle phones (§5.3). The main claim, that a visually driven segmental vocoder is "a reasonable approach for making an SSI" (§5.3), rests on that test, while the authors state that about 60% phone accuracy is not enough for intelligible synthesis (§6); system output from recognized phones is not measured, and all data are uttered speech from two speakers (§2).
